name: Ozone bath (slimming)

card.summary: A mid-century heat-and-moisture cabinet or bath treatment claimed to aid weight loss and skin detoxification.
card.note: Regulators such as the FDA regard ozone as a toxic gas.

quick.overview:
Ozone baths were offered by salons as heat-and-moisture treatments said to slim the body and clear the skin. The appeal was a slimmer figure and clearer skin.

Temporary water loss is the usual effect of steam sessions; ozone itself is regulated as a toxic gas.
quick.how: Clients sat in a steam cabinet or bath, in sessions at a salon.
quick.risks: The FDA calls ozone a toxic gas with no known medical application, and ozone therapies have caused serious harm.

lead: The ozone bath was a salon treatment combining heat, moisture and ozone, said to help weight loss and to detoxify the skin.[1] Clients hoped for a slimmer figure and clearer skin.[1]
The FDA calls ozone a toxic gas with no known useful medical application, and the Wikipedia article on ozone therapy lists documented harms such as pulmonary edema.[1]

angle.text: Practitioners claimed it slimmed and cleared the skin; ozone's role in this has not been studied.

infobox: FDA: ozone toxic, no medical use

paras: Ozone therapies have caused gas embolisms, heart attacks and pulmonary edema, the most common serious effect.[1]
